Fixed. The issue had two causes, both now corrected:

1. **`include/fmt/core.h:1949`** (`specs_setter::on_zero`): the `'0'` flag unconditionally overwrote an explicitly parsed alignment with `align::numeric`. Now it only applies when no alignment was specified (`if (specs_.align == align::none) specs_.align = align::numeric;`), so `{:<+06}` keeps left alignment.

2. **`include/fmt/format.h`** (`write_nonfinite`): zero-padding was applied to inf/nan (producing `'00+nan'`). Now, when the fill is `'0'`, it is replaced with a space before padding (and `numeric` alignment falls back to default right-alignment), matching the documented behavior that zero-padding has no effect on infinity and NaN.

Verification: `format_test.format_nan` and `format_test.format_infinity` now pass, and the full test suite (all 18 ctest targets, including format, core, printf, chrono, wchar tests) passes at 100%.
